property_summary: For any caller and any candidate address, after setOwner(newOwner) succeeds the contract's owner must equal exactly the address passed in; the buggy version instead sets owner to the caller, breaking this for any newOwner different from the caller.

For any caller and any argument, setOwner(newOwner) must set owner exactly to newOwner and change nothing else; the mutant instead overwrites owner with msg.sender, so for any caller other than newOwner the resulting owner differs from the requested value.

After any successful ownership transfer to x, a subsequent call to setOwner(y) made by x must succeed and set owner to y; the mutant steals ownership to the first caller, so x's follow-up call reverts.

For any caller and any requested newOwner, a successful setOwner call must end with owner set exactly to the requested newOwner (not silently to the caller); the mutant leaves owner equal to the caller whenever the caller passes any other target, breaking the rule.

For any fuzzed address a different from the current owner, a successful setOwner(a) must revoke the previous owner's privilege so that the previous owner can no longer call setOwner; the mutant silently keeps ownership at the caller, so the previous owner still succeeds.

For any caller authorized as owner and any requested newOwner, a successful setOwner must leave owner exactly equal to the requested newOwner; note, however, that in this mutant the modifier's `owner = msg.sender` is immediately overwritten by the function body's `owner = _owner`, so the observable final state and return values coincide with the reference for every input and no purely external assertion can separate them — the strongest universal rule is asserted below.

For every candidate address including the zero address, the owner can transfer ownership to it and c.owner() equals that address afterwards; the mutant wrongly reverts when the candidate is address(0).

For any caller acting as owner and any new owner address, a successful setOwner(newOwner) must set owner to exactly newOwner; the mutant instead sets owner to address(this), violating the rule for any input with newOwner != address(c).
